questions.question: As per the Ministry of Finance, what percentage of India's population filed income tax returns in FY 2023-24?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6.68%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per the Ministry of Finance, only **6**.**68%** of India's population filed income tax returns in the financial year 2023-24.
 
• This statistic highlights the **low tax compliance** rate in India despite a growing population and economy.
 
• The filing of income tax returns is mandatory for individuals whose income exceeds the basic exemption limit specified by the government.
 
• In recent years, the government has taken steps to **expand the tax base**, such as digitization and linking PAN with Aadhaar.
 
• The figure indicates that a large portion of the workforce, particularly in the **informal sector**, remains outside the tax net.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Income Tax in India:**

 
 
• Income tax is a direct tax levied by the government on individuals and entities based on their income.
 
• The tax rates are defined under various slabs, with progressive rates for higher income brackets.
 
• For individuals below 60 years of age, the basic exemption limit is ₹2.5 lakh annually.
 
 
 
• **Reasons for Low Tax Compliance:**
 
 
• India has a large **informal economy**, where many individuals earn below the taxable limit.
 
• Lack of awareness about tax laws and compliance requirements in rural and semi-urban areas.
 
• Tax evasion and underreporting of income by certain individuals and entities.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives to Increase Tax Compliance:**
 
 
• The introduction of **faceless assessment** to make tax filing more transparent and less cumbersome.
 
• Implementation of GST (Goods and Services Tax) for better revenue tracking across sectors.
 
• Mandatory linking of PAN with Aadhaar to curb tax evasion.
 
• Awareness campaigns to educate citizens about the importance of filing income tax returns.
 
 
 
• **Role of Informal Sector:**
 
 
• A significant portion of India's workforce is engaged in the informal sector, which typically remains untaxed.
 
• Efforts to formalize the sector include schemes like **PM-KISAN** and digitization drives.

questions.question: In April 2025, India's trade deficit with which country widened to a record $99.2 billion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**China**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India's trade deficit with China widened to a record $99.2 billion in April 2025 due to increasing imports and reduced exports.
 
• China remains India's largest trading partner, primarily exporting electronics, machinery, chemicals, and other manufactured goods to India.
 
• India's exports to China include raw materials like iron ore, cotton, and organic chemicals, but they are significantly lower in comparison to imports.
 
• The trade imbalance is a persistent issue, driven by India's dependency on Chinese goods for industrial and consumer use.
 
• Efforts have been made by India to reduce reliance on Chinese imports, such as promoting domestic manufacturing through initiatives like "Make in India."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Trade Deficit:**

 
 
• A trade deficit occurs when a country's imports exceed its exports in terms of value.
 
• It indicates higher dependency on foreign goods and can impact the country's foreign exchange reserves.
 
 
 
• **India-China Trade Relations:**
 
 
• China is one of India’s largest trading partners, but the relationship is marked by a significant trade imbalance.
 
• India has been trying to diversify its trade partners and reduce dependence on Chinese imports.
 
 
 
• **Make in India Initiative:**
 
 
• Launched in 2014, it aims to boost domestic manufacturing and reduce reliance on imported goods.
 
• Promotes investment in sectors like electronics, machinery, and infrastructure to strengthen domestic capabilities.
 
 
 
• **Key Imported Goods from China:**
 
 
• Electronics and machinery form a major chunk of imports from China to India.
 
• Other imports include chemicals, plastics, and medical equipment.

questions.question: During the 2025 defense expo, Gallium Nitride (GaN) Semiconductor Solutions was highlighted as a key advancement in which area of defense technology?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Radar and electronic warfare systems**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Gallium Nitride (GaN)** is a semiconductor material known for its ability to operate at high power and high frequency, making it ideal for defense applications.
 
• GaN technology is widely used in **radar systems** due to its efficiency in generating high-frequency signals and improved detection capabilities.
 
• In electronic warfare, GaN-based systems offer **higher power density, thermal conductivity, and reliability**, enhancing the performance of jammers and signal processors.
 
• GaN semiconductors enable **compact and lightweight designs**, which are crucial for modern defense platforms like drones, fighter aircraft, and naval vessels.
 
• Countries across the globe are investing in GaN-based radar and electronic warfare systems for **advanced threat detection and response capabilities**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gallium Nitride (GaN) Material Properties**

 
 
• GaN has a wide bandgap of 3.4 eV, enabling it to operate at high voltages and temperatures.
 
• It exhibits excellent thermal conductivity, which reduces overheating risks in high-power applications.
 
• GaN transistors are 10 times faster than silicon-based alternatives, making them ideal for high-frequency operations.
 
 
 
• **Applications in Radar Systems**
 
 
• GaN-based radars provide enhanced range, resolution, and reliability, crucial for air and missile defense systems.
 
• They are used in Active Electronically Scanned Array (AESA) radars for advanced situational awareness.
 
 
 
• **Electronic Warfare Systems**
 
 
• GaN amplifiers are essential for high-power jamming systems, ensuring effective disruption of enemy communication.
 
• They support signal intelligence (SIGINT) and electronic countermeasures (ECM) to protect military assets.
 
 
 
• **Global Investment in GaN Technology**
 
 
• Countries like the USA, China, and India are heavily investing in GaN-based systems for modernizing their defense infrastructure.
 
• GaN technology is a key enabler for next-generation defense platforms such as hypersonic weapons and space-based radars.

questions.question: In April 2025, in which city of India did the Central Zoo Authority (CZA) approve the city's first deer park?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Noida**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In April 2025, the Central Zoo Authority (CZA) approved the establishment of Noida's first deer park.
 
• The park is aimed at promoting wildlife conservation and providing a habitat for various deer species.
 
• The deer park will also serve as an educational and recreational facility for visitors, highlighting the importance of biodiversity conservation.
 
• Noida's initiative aligns with India’s broader goal of enhancing urban green spaces and wildlife preservation efforts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Central Zoo Authority (CZA):**

 
 
• The CZA is a statutory body under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India.
 
• It was established in 1992 to oversee the management of zoos in India and ensure the welfare of captive animals.
 
• The authority plays a crucial role in approving zoo projects and monitoring their compliance with prescribed standards.
 
 
 
• **Deer Conservation in India:**
 
 
• India is home to a variety of deer species, including the spotted deer (chital), swamp deer (barasingha), and sambar deer.
 
• These species play a vital role in maintaining the ecological balance of forest ecosystems.
 
• Conservation measures are critical as some deer species face threats from habitat loss and poaching.
 
 
 
• **Urban Green Spaces:**
 
 
• Urban green spaces like parks, gardens, and wildlife reserves contribute to sustainable urban development.
 
• They improve air quality, provide recreational opportunities, and promote mental well-being.
 
• Initiatives like deer parks in urban areas encourage environmental awareness among city dwellers.
 
 
 
• **Biodiversity in India:**
 
 
• India is one of the 17 megadiverse countries in the world, hosting over 7% of the world’s biodiversity.
 
• Conservation efforts in urban and rural areas are crucial to preserving this rich biodiversity.
 
• Projects like the Noida deer park highlight the importance of integrating biodiversity conservation into urban planning.

questions.question: What is the setting for Alice Feeney’s 2025 psychological thriller Beautiful Ugly?

questions.solution:

__
 
• **Beautiful Ugly**, Alice Feeney’s 2025 psychological thriller, is set on a **remote Scottish island**.
 
• The island's isolated and eerie environment serves as the perfect backdrop for the novel's dark and suspenseful themes.

• The setting plays a significant role in creating a claustrophobic and mysterious atmosphere, intensifying the psychological tension.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The setting provides the backdrop against which a story unfolds, influencing the mood, theme, and character development.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements regarding the Uttar Poorva Transformative Industrialization Scheme (UNNATI), as highlighted in Rajya Sabha Unstarred Question

(answered on 20 December 2024), is/are correct?

The total budget outlay for the UNNATI Scheme is ₹10,037 crores, with 60% of the outlay allocated to the North East Region.

Capital Investment Incentives in Zone A districts are higher than in Zone B districts.

The UNNATI Scheme is effective for 10 years, with an additional 8 years for meeting committed liabilities.

The UNNATI Scheme is a Central sector scheme implemented under the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 and 3 Only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Under the **UNNATI scheme** the total budget outlay of the Scheme is **Rs 10,037 cr**.
 
• The total budget outlay is divided into two parts – Part A and Part B.
 
 
• **Part A **of the scheme, with an outlay of **Rs 9,737 cr**., if for providing incentives to eligible new industrial units and those undergoing substantial expansion.
 
• **Part B** of the scheme, with an outlay of **Rs 300 cr**. is for implementation & institutional arrangements for the scheme.
 
 
 
• **60% **of the scheme outlay of part A is earmarked to all States of North Eastern Region (NER).
 
• The districts are categorized in two zones: **Zone A (industrially advanced districts) and Zone B (industrially backwards districts)** based on NER district SDG index (2021-22).
 
• It is a **Central Sector Scheme** implemented under the** Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)** in cooperation with the states.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Central Sector Scheme**

 
 
• These schemes are fully funded by the Central Government and implemented by central agencies.
 
• They are designed to address national priorities, such as infrastructure development, social welfare, and economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Capital Investment Incentives**
 
 
• These are financial benefits provided to investors to encourage infrastructure development and industrialization.
 
• In the UNNATI Scheme, Zone A districts receive higher incentives compared to Zone B districts to attract investments in strategic areas.
 
 
 
• **North East Region (NER) Development**
 
 
• The NER comprises eight states: Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, and Tripura.
 
• Special attention is given to this region to promote economic growth, employment generation, and industrialization.
 
 
 
• **Committed Liabilities**
 
 
• This term refers to financial obligations that the government must honor based on previously approved projects or agreements.
 
• The UNNATI Scheme allows an extended period of 8 years beyond its effective duration to fulfill such liabilities.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region**
 
 
• Established in 2001, the ministry is responsible for planning, executing, and monitoring development projects in the North East Region.
 
• It works to bridge the gap in infrastructure and socio-economic development in the region.

questions.question: In March 2025, India's Parliament passed the Bills of Lading Bill, 2025. What was the primary objective of this legislation?

options.text: To modernise the 169 years old shipping law

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To modernise the 169 years old shipping law**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India's Parliament passed the **Bills of Lading Bill, 2025** to modernise the **169-year-old shipping laws** and align them with current international shipping practices.
 
• The bill replaces the **Indian Bills of Lading Act, 1856**, which was outdated and did not reflect advancements in the shipping industry.
 
• The legislation introduces **digital bills of lading**, allowing electronic documentation and reducing the dependency on physical paperwork in maritime trade.
 
• It aims to boost **efficiency and transparency** in maritime logistics, facilitating faster and more secure trade documentation processes.
 
• The new framework ensures India's shipping laws comply with **global maritime conventions**, fostering better trade relationships with international partners.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bills of Lading:**

 
 
• A bill of lading is a legal document issued by a carrier to a shipper, detailing the type, quantity, and destination of goods being transported.
 
• It serves as proof of shipment, a receipt of goods, and a document of title, enabling ownership transfer during trade.
 
 
 
• **Indian Bills of Lading Act, 1856:**
 
 
• This act governed bills of lading in India for over 169 years, but was increasingly inadequate for modern maritime trade needs.
 
• The act lacked provisions for electronic documentation and modern dispute resolution mechanisms.
 
 
 
• **Digital Bills of Lading:**
 
 
• Digital bills of lading enable electronic issuance, transfer, and verification of documents, reducing fraud and operational delays.
 
• This shift aligns with global trends in **e-commerce and digitisation of trade**.
 
 
 
• **Global Maritime Trade:**
 
 
• The shipping industry handles approximately **80% of global trade** by volume, making efficient legislation critical for economic growth.
 
• Modern laws ensure compliance with conventions like the **United Nations Convention on the Carriage of Goods by Sea** (Hamburg Rules).

questions.question: As per IMF’s January 2025 report, what is the projected global headline inflation rate for 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4.2%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) January 2025 report, **the projected global headline inflation rate for 2025 is 4.2%.**
 
• Global headline inflation reflects the overall inflation rate across the world, considering both advanced and emerging economies.
 
• IMF projections are based on comprehensive economic models and data analysis from member countries.
 
• Factors contributing to the 2025 inflation projection include **monetary policies, geopolitical tensions, supply chain disruptions, and energy market dynamics.**
 
• The IMF’s report serves as a critical reference for policymakers and economists to shape economic strategies globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Headline Inflation:**

 
 
• It measures the total inflation within an economy, including volatile elements such as food and energy prices.
 
• Unlike core inflation, headline inflation does not exclude specific categories like energy and food.
 
 
 
• **IMF and Inflation Projections:**
 
 
• The IMF publishes inflation forecasts in its World Economic Outlook reports, which are released several times a year.
 
• These forecasts are essential for global economic planning and policymaking.
 
 
 
• **Factors Influencing Global Inflation:**
 
 
• Key factors include supply chain challenges, monetary policies, energy price fluctuations, and geopolitical instability.
 
• Central banks worldwide adjust interest rates to manage inflation levels effectively.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Inflation:**
 
 
• High inflation decreases purchasing power and increases the cost of living.
 
• Conversely, deflation (negative inflation) can lead to economic stagnation.

questions.question: As of April 2025, how many languages are listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**22**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution lists **22 recognized languages** as of April 2025.
 
• This schedule was initially adopted in 1950 with **14 languages** listed.
 
• Subsequent amendments, including the 71st and 92nd Constitutional Amendments, added **Sindhi, Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali, Bodo, Santhali, Maithili, and Dogri**.
 
• The recognized languages include major regional languages such as Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, Marathi, Urdu, and Punjabi, among others.
 
• The inclusion of languages in the Eighth Schedule allows for their use in official communication, education, and legislative processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eighth Schedule Overview:**

 
 
• The Eighth Schedule is part of the Indian Constitution, which enumerates languages recognized by the government.
 
• It primarily aims to promote linguistic diversity and protect regional languages.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Amendments:**
 
 
• The 71st Amendment in 1992 added Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali to the Eighth Schedule.
 
• The 92nd Amendment in 2003 included Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali.
 
 
 
• **Official Language Policy:**
 
 
• Hindi, listed in the Eighth Schedule, is designated as the **official language of India**.
 
• English is used for official purposes along with Hindi under Article 343.
 
 
 
• **India's Linguistic Diversity:**
 
 
• India is one of the most linguistically diverse countries, with over **19,500 dialects** spoken as per the Census of India.
 
• The recognition of languages in the Eighth Schedule ensures government support for their preservation and promotion.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Recognition:**
 
 
• Recognized languages can be used in competitive exams, official communication, and legislative debates.
 
• They receive funding and resources for their development, including translation services and literature promotion.

Jawaharlal Nehru Indoor Stadium and Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium

__
 
• The Khelo India Para Games (KIPG) 2025 was held at **Jawaharlal Nehru Indoor Stadium, Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium, and Dr Karni Singh Shooting Range**, which are prominent sports venues in India.
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru Indoor Stadium** is located in Delhi and is a multi-purpose indoor sports venue known for hosting large-scale national and international events.
 
• **Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium**, also situated in Delhi, is one of the largest indoor stadiums in India and is frequently used for multi-sport competitions.
 
• **Dr Karni Singh Shooting Range**, located in New Delhi, is a world-class shooting range used for major shooting championships and training.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khelo India Programme:**

 
 
• Khelo India is a national sports development initiative launched by the Government of India to promote sports culture at the grassroots level and encourage young talent.
 
• The programme focuses on infrastructure development, athlete training, and enhancing participation in sports across all age groups.
 
 
 
• **Para Sports in India:**
 
 
• Para sports are adapted sports designed for athletes with physical and intellectual disabilities.

• Named after Maharaja Karni Singh of Bikaner, the range is a state-of-the-art facility for shooting sports.

questions.question: Who among the following has become the 11th Chairman of Securities and Exchange Board of India in February 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tuhin Kanta Pandey**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Tuhin Kanta Pandey** was appointed as the 11th Chairman of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) in February 2025.
 
• He succeeded the outgoing SEBI chairman, **Madhabi Puri Buch**, who served from 2022 to 2025.
 
• Tuhin Kanta Pandey is an Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer of the **1987 Odisha cadre**.
 
• Before his appointment as SEBI Chairman, he served as the Secretary of the Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM).
 
• As SEBI Chairman, his role involves regulating and promoting the securities market in India while protecting the interests of investors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI):**

 
 
• SEBI is the regulatory body for the securities and commodity market in India under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Finance.
 
• It was established in 1988 and given statutory powers through the SEBI Act, 1992.
 
• SEBI’s primary function is to protect investor interests, promote the development of the securities market, and regulate its functioning.
 
 
 
• **Role of SEBI Chairman:**
 
 
• The SEBI Chairman is responsible for overseeing the functioning of the Indian securities and commodity markets.
 
• They ensure compliance with regulations, protect investors, and facilitate the growth of capital markets.
 
 
 
• **Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM):**
 
 
• DIPAM is responsible for managing the government’s investments in public sector undertakings (PSUs) and facilitating their disinvestment.
 
• Tuhin Kanta Pandey played a key role in the strategic disinvestments of major PSUs during his tenure as DIPAM Secretary.
 
 
 
• **Previous SEBI Chairpersons:**
 
 
• Notable past chairpersons include U.K. Sinha, Ajay Tyagi, and Madhabi Puri Buch.
 
• Madhabi Puri Buch was the first female Chairperson of SEBI, serving from 2022 to 2025.

questions.question: Who among the following was awarded the Grand Collar of the Timor-Leste in August 2024?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Droupadi Murmu**, the President of India, was awarded the **Grand Collar of the Order of Timor-Leste** in August 2024.
 
• This is the **highest civilian honor** of Timor-Leste, conferred to individuals for their significant contributions to strengthening bilateral ties.
 
• The honor was bestowed during her state visit to Timor-Leste, aimed at enhancing diplomatic and economic relations between the two nations.
 
• This was the first state visit by an Indian President to Timor-Leste, marking a historic milestone in India-Timor-Leste relations.
 
• The award reflects India’s growing global recognition and the emphasis placed on fostering international partnerships.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Grand Collar of the Order of Timor-Leste**:

 
 
• This is the highest distinction given by the Government of Timor-Leste to individuals who have significantly contributed to the country's development or international relations.
 
• Previous recipients include heads of state and other global leaders who have supported Timor-Leste's growth and international standing.
 
 
 
• **India-Timor-Leste Relations**:
 
 
• Diplomatic relations between India and Timor-Leste were established in 2003, shortly after Timor-Leste's independence in 2002.
 
• India has supported Timor-Leste in areas like capacity building, economic development, and infrastructure development.

questions.question: In January 2025, who became the first Indian to be nominated for Best Director (Motion Picture) at the Golden Globe Awards?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Payal Kapadia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Payal Kapadia became the first Indian filmmaker nominated for the **Best Director (Motion Picture)** category at the **Golden Globe Awards** in January 2025.
 
• Her nomination came for her critically acclaimed work, which showcased **innovative storytelling and unique cinematic techniques**.
 
• Payal Kapadia gained international recognition with her previous documentary **"A Night of Knowing Nothing,"** which won the **Golden Eye Award** at the Cannes Film Festival.
 
• The Golden Globe Awards are globally renowned and considered one of the most prestigious platforms for recognizing excellence in film and television.
 
• Her nomination marked a historic milestone for Indian cinema, highlighting the growing influence of Indian filmmakers on the global stage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Golden Globe Awards:**

 
 
• Established in 1944, the Golden Globe Awards are presented by the Hollywood Foreign Press Association (HFPA).
 
• The awards recognize outstanding achievements in film and television across various categories such as acting, directing, and screenwriting.
 
• They are considered a precursor to the Oscars, often influencing the Academy Awards nominations and winners.
 
 
 
• **Payal Kapadia:**
 
 
• She is an Indian filmmaker known for her experimental and thought-provoking narratives.
 
• Her works often explore themes of identity, societal challenges, and personal relationships.
 
• Kapadia is an alumnus of the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), Pune, where she honed her craft.
 
 
 
• **"A Night of Knowing Nothing":**

questions.question: Who among the following is NOT eligible for the subsidy under the PMAY-U 2.0 scheme launched in 2024?

options.text: Middle Income Groups (MIG) having an annual income of up to ₹9 lakh per year

questions.solution:

questions.question: Anti-dumping and anti-subsidies & countervailing measures in India are administered by which Ministry?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Commerce and Industry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Anti-dumping and anti-subsidy measures are administered by the Directorate General of Trade Remedies (**DGTR**), which operates under the **Ministry of Commerce and Industry**.
 
• The Directorate General of Trade Remedies (DGTR) is responsible for investigations and recommendations on anti-dumping duties, countervailing duties, and safeguard measures.
 
• Anti-dumping measures are implemented to protect domestic industries from **unfair trade practices** such as dumping, where goods are exported at prices lower than their normal value.
 
• Countervailing measures are aimed at offsetting subsidies provided by the exporting country's government, ensuring fair competition for domestic producers.
 
• The Ministry of Commerce and Industry's role is to ensure compliance with WTO regulations while safeguarding Indian industries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Anti-Dumping:**

 
 
• Dumping refers to the practice of exporting goods at a price lower than their normal value in the domestic market.
 
• Anti-dumping measures are permitted under the rules of the **World Trade Organization (WTO)**.
 
• The goal is to protect domestic industries from material injury caused by unfair pricing.
 
 
 
• **Countervailing Measures:**
 
 
• Countervailing duties are tariffs imposed to counteract subsidies provided by exporting countries to their producers.
 
• These measures ensure a level playing field for domestic industries.
 
 
 
• **Directorate General of Trade Remedies (DGTR):**
 
 
• The DGTR was established in 2018 as an integrated authority for administering trade remedy measures.
 
• It consolidates the functions of anti-dumping, countervailing, and safeguard investigations under one body.
 
 
 
• **World Trade Organization (WTO) Compliance:**
 
 
• India's trade remedy measures are aligned with WTO agreements, such as the Agreement on Anti-Dumping and the Agreement on Subsidies and Countervailing Measures.
 
• These measures aim to promote fair trade while adhering to international norms.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the December 2024 appointments to the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) is INCORRECT?

options.text: Justice V Ramasubramanian was appointed as the Chairperson of NHRC.
Shri Priyank Kanoongo was appointed as the Secretary General of NHRC.
Justice (Dr.) Bidyut Ranjan Sarangi joined NHRC as a Member.
The appointments were made by the President of India in December 2024.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shri Priyank Kanoongo was appointed as the Secretary General of NHRC**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) is an independent statutory body established under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.
 
• Justice V Ramasubramanian's appointment as Chairperson aligns with the NHRC's mandate of appointing a retired Chief Justice of India or a Judge of the Supreme Court as Chairperson.
 
• Justice (Dr.) Bidyut Ranjan Sarangi has been confirmed as a Member of NHRC in December 2024.
 
• All appointments to the NHRC, including Chairperson and Members, are made by the President of India based on recommendations from a committee chaired by the Prime Minister.
 
• Shri Priyank Kanoongo is currently the Chairperson of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) and has not been appointed as the Secretary General of NHRC.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **NHRC Composition:**

 
 
• The NHRC consists of a Chairperson, Members, and Ex-officio Members, including Chairpersons of National Commissions like SC/ST, Women, Minorities, etc.
 
• The Chairperson is typically a retired Chief Justice or a Judge of the Supreme Court.
 
 
 
• **Appointment Process:**
 
 
• Appointments are made by the President of India based on recommendations from a high-level committee chaired by the Prime Minister.
 
• The committee includes the Union Home Minister, Leaders of Opposition in Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, and others.
 
 
 
• **Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993:**
 
 
• This Act provides the legal framework for establishing the NHRC and State Human Rights Commissions.
 
• The Act aims to protect and promote human rights guaranteed by the Constitution and embodied in international covenants.
 
 
 
• **Role of NHRC:**
 
 
• NHRC investigates human rights violations and recommends measures to ensure compliance with constitutional and legal rights.
 
• It submits annual reports to the President of India and can intervene in court cases involving human rights violations.

questions.question: In which of the following countries did the United Nations Biodiversity Convention 2024 (COP16) conclude in February 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Colombia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The United Nations Biodiversity Conference (COP16) is scheduled to be held in **Colombia** in February 2025.
 
• Colombia, known for its rich biodiversity, was chosen to host this crucial event, emphasizing its role in global biodiversity conservation.
 
• The conference is a part of the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), which aims to promote sustainable development and address global biodiversity loss.
 
• Previous COPs under the CBD have focused on the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, which sets targets for biodiversity protection until 2030.
 
• The event will bring together governments, scientists, and stakeholders to discuss and implement strategies for biodiversity conservation and sustainable use of natural resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD):**

 
 
• The CBD is an international treaty adopted at the Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro in 1992.
 
• Its primary objectives include the conservation of biodiversity, sustainable use of its components, and fair sharing of benefits from genetic resources.
 
• It has been ratified by 196 parties, making it a near-universal environmental agreement.
 
 
 
• **Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework:**
 
 
• Adopted during COP15 in 2022, this framework sets 23 global targets to halt and reverse biodiversity loss by 2030.
 
• Key targets include protecting 30% of the planet's land and oceans and restoring degraded ecosystems.
 
 
 
• **Biodiversity Hotspots:**
 
 
• Colombia is one of the world's most biodiverse countries, hosting a significant portion of the Amazon rainforest, Andes mountain range, and Orinoco plains.
 
• It is home to 10% of the planet’s species, making it a critical location for global biodiversity conservation efforts.
 
 
 
• **Previous COP Locations:**
 
 
• COP15 was held in two parts: Kunming, China (2021), and Montreal, Canada (2022).
 
• COP14 was hosted in Sharm El-Sheikh, Egypt, in 2018.
 
 
 
• **Role of COP16:**
 
 
• COP16 will review the progress made under the Kunming-Montreal framework and address emerging issues in biodiversity conservation.
 
• It will also provide a platform for nations to discuss financing mechanisms and partnerships for achieving biodiversity targets.

questions.question: Which of the following banks has reported a significant rise in its net short position in the forward book, which expanded to $77.5 billion by the end of January 2025, up from $67.9 billion in December 2024?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) reported a significant rise in its net short position in the forward book, expanding to **$77.5 billion** by the end of January 2025, from **$67.9 billion** in December 2024.
 
• RBI’s forward book reflects its activity in managing foreign exchange reserves and hedging against currency risks.
 
• A net short position in the forward book indicates that the RBI has sold more foreign exchange forward contracts than it has purchased.
 
• This rise in the net short position could be indicative of RBI’s strategy to manage exchange rate volatility and ensure stability in the currency market.
 
• The forward book positions are closely monitored to assess the central bank’s approach towards external sector management.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Forward Contracts:** Financial agreements where two parties agree to exchange a specific amount of currency at a predetermined rate on a future date.
 
• **Net Short Position:** Occurs when an entity has sold more of a financial instrument than it has purchased, indicating a bearish outlook or hedging strategy.
 
• **Foreign Exchange Reserves:** Assets held by a central bank in foreign currencies, used to back liabilities and stabilize the national currency.
 
• **Currency Hedging:** A strategy to protect against exchange rate fluctuations, ensuring stability in international transactions.
 
• **RBI's Role:** The Reserve Bank of India actively manages the foreign exchange market to ensure liquidity, reduce volatility, and maintain economic stability.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a change of the new Income Tax bill introduced in the Parliament during February 2025?

options.text: Reorganisation of sections logically to facilitate ease of reference
Deletion of existing taxation principles, without ensuring continuity and usability
Elimination of intricate language to enhance readability
Removal of redundant and repetitive provisions for better navigation

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deletion of existing taxation principles, without ensuring continuity and usability**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The new Income Tax Bill introduced in February 2025 focuses on **reorganizing sections logically** to make them easier to reference and understand.
 
• The bill emphasizes **eliminating intricate language** and introducing simpler terminology to enhance readability for taxpayers.
 
• **Redundant and repetitive provisions** have been removed to improve navigational efficiency within the tax code.
 
• Contrary to the claim in the incorrect option, the bill does not delete existing taxation principles arbitrarily. It ensures **continuity and usability** of critical provisions.
 
• The overarching aim of these changes is to create a more taxpayer-friendly system that aligns with modern requirements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reorganization of Sections:** The restructuring of tax laws aims to make the system more intuitive, grouping related provisions together for better coherence.
 
• **Ease of Compliance:** Simplified language and logical arrangements reduce the burden of compliance and improve accessibility for taxpayers.
 
• **Taxation Principles:** These are the core rules and guidelines governing the tax system, including concepts like income classification, deduction eligibility, and tax computation.
 
• **Redundant Provisions:** These are outdated or repetitive rules that no longer serve a purpose and have been removed to streamline the legal framework.
 
• **Modernization of Tax Laws:** The bill reflects efforts to align tax regulations with current economic and technological developments, facilitating digital transactions and transparency.

questions.question: In March 2025, the theme of the 54th National Safety Week focused on which of the following?

options.text: Safety & Well-being Crucial for Viksit Bharat

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Safety & Well-being Crucial for Viksit Bharat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The 54th National Safety Week, held in March 2025, emphasized the theme **"Safety & Well-being Crucial for Viksit Bharat."**
 
• This theme aligns with India's vision of becoming a developed nation ("Viksit Bharat") through prioritizing workplace safety and overall well-being.
 
• National Safety Week is organized by the **National Safety Council (NSC)**, aiming to raise awareness about safety, health, and environmental issues.
 
• Activities during the week include workshops, training sessions, safety audits, and campaigns to promote a culture of safety across industries.
 
• The initiative highlights the importance of integrating safety measures at all organizational levels to ensure sustainable growth and development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Safety Council (NSC):** Established in 1966, NSC is an autonomous body under the Ministry of Labour and Employment dedicated to promoting safety awareness in India.
 
• **Safety Week Goals:** The event aims to reduce workplace accidents, improve health standards, and foster a preventive culture in industries.
 
• **Viksit Bharat Vision:** "Viksit Bharat" refers to India's developmental goals, focusing on advanced infrastructure, human resource development, and sustainable practices.
 
• **Well-being in Workplace:** Includes mental health support, ergonomic measures, and ensuring safe working conditions to enhance productivity and employee satisfaction.
 
• **Safety Audits:** A systematic evaluation of workplace safety practices and compliance with statutory regulations to identify and mitigate risks.

questions.question: In April 2025, the DRDO and the Indian Army successfully conducted four flight-tests of which missile system from Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Medium-Range Surface-to-Air Missile (MRSAM)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Medium-Range Surface-to-Air Missile (MRSAM)** is an advanced air defense missile system developed jointly by the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** and **Israel Aerospace Industries (IAI)**.
 
• The missile system successfully conducted **four flight-tests** in April 2025 from the **Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Island** off the coast of Odisha, India.
 
• MRSAM is designed to provide **multi-layered air defense** against enemy aircraft, missiles, and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs).
 
• The system has a range of approximately **70 kilometers** and features **advanced radar, command-and-control systems, and mobile launchers**.
 
• It is a critical component of India’s defense capabilities, aimed at strengthening airspace security for the Indian Army, Navy, and Air Force.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Island:** Formerly known as Wheeler Island, it is an integrated test range for missile systems located in Odisha, used for testing various indigenous and strategic missile systems.
 
• **Features of MRSAM:** Includes advanced phased-array radar, interceptor missiles with advanced guidance, and a mobile launcher system to ensure high precision and mobility.
 
• **Collaborative Development:** MRSAM is a joint venture between DRDO and IAI, showcasing India-Israel defense cooperation in missile technology.
 
• **Operational Role:** The system is tailored for both offensive and defensive roles, capable of neutralizing aerial threats in diverse combat scenarios.
 
• **Previous Tests:** MRSAM has undergone multiple successful tests since its inception, validating its performance and reliability under various operational conditions.
